charters: Explore refunds across every reason, partial amounts and currencies to discover where the six recent fixes left gaps
Explore paying with a gift card plus a card, including a card that covers the whole order

test_types.why: Checkout and refund are the P0 journey; automate the card and refund paths end to end.
Six fix commits in six months, five of them on refunds or currency: explore around them.
The gateway is an external HTTP API; pin the charge and refund request shapes.
The two payments tests only check rejections; measure what the refund and fee logic tests miss.

charters: Explore issuing and redeeming gift cards at the $5 and $500 limits and redeeming more than the balance

test_types.why: New in this release with no history and no tests; it sits on the P0 checkout journey because payments now imports it. The charter is ready, but this budget leaves it no session: run it first if any time frees up.
Issue and redeem limits ($5 to $500, partial redemption) need unit tests.
Payments now calls redeem(): run the payments regression suite with gift cards.

not_tested.reason: The 1-session budget covers one High area's floor; auth is the second High area and gets no session. Its open finding F-1 still needs the security retest before release.
Medium risk (8.9), but the single session goes to payments. Catalog keeps its existing test and the browse journey.
Low risk (5.8): highest churn, but banner copy moves no money and touches no account. With one session there is no time for it; its existing test keeps running.
Low risk (3.5): the most complex area, but one 4-line change in six months, no fixes, a P3 admin journey and an existing unit test. Its existing test keeps running in CI.

entry_criteria: The release candidate is deployed to the staging environment with the gateway sandbox.
Security finding F-1 has a fix in the release candidate, or an accepted exception.
Gift card issue and redeem are feature-complete and behind no flag in staging.

exit_criteria.condition: Every High-risk area's planned sessions are done and their charters debriefed
exit_criteria.measure: session sheets for payments and auth

exit_criteria.condition: No open critical or high defect in payments, auth or gift cards
exit_criteria.measure: defect tracker query for this release

exit_criteria.condition: The checkout and sign-in journeys pass in staging

assumptions: Fix commits are found by message (a fix:, hotfix: or revert: type, or a subject starting with fix, bugfix, hotfix, revert or regression, or naming a bug); merges are not counted, and a fix with another message is missed.
Reach comes from the journey graph, because no usage export was given.
The journey map predates gift cards; they reach the P0 checkout journey only through the payments service's import, so their journey criticality rests on that one link until the map is refreshed.
open_questions: Should gift cards get a journey in the journey map before release? Run journey-mapper.
Is the stock report used outside head office? If so, reports may deserve more than its existing test.

summary.headline: One session is 1 session short of the High floors: it goes to payments. Auth (High, open finding F-1) is left untested on purpose and needs someone to accept that; gift cards are planned but get no session of their own.
